description: Who slept where, and between which dates. The record persists after the person leaves: an assignment that is deleted when it ends cannot defend an IRS Section 119 classification, cannot answer a wage claim about a housing deduction, and cannot tell a food safety investigator who was in the camp the week in question.

fields.description: The unit this person was housed in.
fields.label: Housing Unit

fields.description: v0.327.0. Which room of the unit, where it has rooms (a duplex: 16a / 16b). Must be one of the unit's Room Labels.
fields.label: Room

fields.description: The Employee, where Frappe HR is installed. Where it is not, the tools record the name in Employee Name and leave this blank — a camp roster that cannot be written until an HR module is installed is a camp roster nobody keeps.
fields.label: Employee

fields.description: The person's name as the roster has it. Copied from the Employee record when there is one, so a report reads without a join and so the record survives an Employee being renamed.
fields.label: Employee Name

fields.description: Blank means currently assigned. That is the whole occupancy model: there is no separate 'active' flag to fall out of step with the dates.
fields.label: End Date

fields.description: Derived from the dates on every save, so a filter and a report can use it. Never set by hand — the dates are the record and this is a reading of them.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: What went back when the assignment ended. A deposit returned that exceeds the deposit paid is refused, because that is a refund of money nobody took.
fields.label: Deposit Returned

fields.description: Whether a housing charge was deducted from this person's wages. ORS 653 and OAR 839-015 constrain when that is lawful and for how much, and the question is asked of the arrangement rather than of the building — which is why it is on the assignment. Unknown is a distinct answer from No and is the honest default.
fields.label: Housing Deduction from Wages

name: Housing Assignment
